A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCONE work. Their complete text, tables, figures, algorithms, and appendices support reliable comparison. The original material can be matched despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model training experiments, downstream accuracy, vocabulary and model-size analyses, and memory and latency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Qwen3 post-training experiments and additional resource measurements in Appendices E.3–E.4.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–4 retain the same frequent n-gram selection, embedding-learning procedure, and precomputed off-accelerator lookups. Appendix E.3 applies SCONE during supervised fine-tuning without specifying a modified algorithm or loss.

E1.justification: v3 adds supervised fine-tuning on Mixture-of-Thoughts and evaluations on AIME 2024 mathematics and LiveCodeBench v4/v5 coding tasks. This substantially extends the earlier pretraining and zero-shot evaluation coverage. Existing datasets and tasks are retained.

E2.justification: New Table 4 adds an evaluated Qwen3-4B-base comparator for the post-training experiment. The original GPT-2, OLMo, and OE-12.8M comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 introduces a supervised fine-tuning protocol with a Qwen3-4B main model, 8B or 14B f-gram models, 10M f-grams, and pass@1 evaluation. E.4 adds resource profiling at context length 2048 and batch size 4 on an A100 80GB. These are additional protocols; the original pretraining settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.3 extends the f-gram model-size analysis to post-training by comparing 8B and 14B variants. E.4 adds a combined analysis of memory, storage, latency, and training compute. The existing n-gram-length, embedding-count, vocabulary, and scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 specifies that Table 5 latency is averaged over 1,000 decoding steps and explicitly discloses in checklist item 7 that large-scale pretraining received no formal significance testing. Existing three-seed averaging and plotted uncertainty are retained. These are reporting additions, without evidence of increased independent training runs or new confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Original result tables and figure findings are unchanged. New Table 4 reports AIME/LiveCodeBench pass@1 scores of 45.3/30.8 for the Qwen baseline, 48.3/34.5 with the 8B f-gram model, and 51.6/36.3 with the 14B model. Table 5 adds resource results, including GPU memory of 8.38, 5.60, and 4.45GB for its three configurations. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, indexing arguments, and formal algorithms are retained with equivalent notation. Neither version presents new theorems or proofs; the added checklist explicitly confirms the absence of new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: two embedding-scaling strategies with fixed inference accelerator requirements, and a 1B accelerator-resident model outperforming a 1.9B baseline. The new experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets the Qwen3 results as evidence of effectiveness during post-training and explicitly acknowledges missing significance testing for large-scale pretraining. Appendix A remains unchanged, leaving its statement that evaluation covers only up to 3B training-time parameters unreconciled with the new Qwen3 experiments.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds framework and dataset links and points to open-r1 training hyperparameters. E.4 documents profiling hardware and conditions. The checklist adds a promise to release code after review, without establishing an actual release. Existing Appendix F implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Qwen3 technical report by Yang et al. for the post-training study. Research positioning in Section 5 and Appendix B is otherwise retained. The over-tokenized transformer's arXiv-to-ICML reference update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering remain unchanged. v3 adds an experimental roadmap, renames Section 4.1, adds Appendices E.3–E.4 and a NeurIPS checklist, and makes limited wording and citation-style edits.

P2.justification: v3 adopts NeurIPS typography and title formatting and reflows figures, tables, and algorithms throughout the document, including grouping Figures 8–10 together. It adds Tables 4–5 and moves Table 2 units into column headings. All 13 original figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The post-training experiments broaden the empirical evidence, while Table 5 makes training and deployment resource tradeoffs easier to assess than v2's separate measurements. These are useful overall gains, limited by sparse post-training protocol details and the unreconciled 3B-only limitation in Appendix A.
